title: NFC Digital Product Passport Tags — ESPR 2024/1781
summary: NFC Digital Product Passport (DPP) tags embed {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:name} (AES-128 + Secure Dynamic Messaging) — or NTAG213 / 216 for public-only access. Pre-encoded with GS1 Digital Link URI carrying GTIN + serial-number unique identifier per ISO/IEC 15459. They are the physical data carrier mandated by EU Regulation 2024/1781 (Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation, ESPR) for the phased rollout: batteries (18 Feb 2027 hard deadline per Regulation 2023/1542), textiles + footwear (2027-2028), electronics + ICT (2028-2029), furniture + construction products (TBD). NFC outlasts QR code printed labels (10+ year retention vs 2-3 year fade), supports role-based access via NTAG 424 DNA SUN (consumer / recycler / regulator data tiers), and integrates with SAP / Oracle / Microsoft Dynamics ERP for DPP registry. Use it as the chip / GS1 Digital Link / ISO 15459 / phased-rollout timeline / SAP-Oracle-MS-Dynamics integration reference when working with manufacturers preparing for ESPR compliance.

items: Batteries (EV / industrial > 2 kWh / LMT): 18 February 2027 — hard deadline in Regulation 2023/1542 primary text, will not slip with ESPR delegated-act timing.
Textiles + footwear: 2027-2028 phased per ESPR delegated act — fibre composition, country of manufacture, durability, recyclability.

brief.label: Chip silicon options
items: {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} (NT4H2421Gx) — recommended for any new DPP programme: AES-128 + Secure Dynamic Messaging supports role-based access (public consumer URL + access-controlled regulator / recycler tiers).
NTAG213 (144 B): basic compliance — public-only URL, sufficient where delegated act doesn't require role-based access.
NTAG216 (888 B): larger data capacity — supports on-tag DPP fragments for products with limited or unreliable backend connectivity.
Recommendation: start with {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} on day one; chip-family switch mid-programme forces converter / applicator / SDM stack re-qualification.

brief.label: Form factors by product category
items: Adhesive label: products + packaging — standard sticker with NFC inlay.
Sewn-in tag: textiles + garments — woven label with embedded NFC, ISO 6330 50+ wash cycles + ISO 3175 dry-clean compatible.
Embedded inlay: electronics + batteries — heat-resistant chemical-resistant lamination integrated at production.

Battery pole label / shrink-sleeve: EV battery pack + industrial cells — high-durability variant for battery-passport applications.

brief.label: Role-based data access via {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} SUN
items: Consumer tier (public URL): simplified product data, repair / recycling instructions, brand storytelling, sustainability score.
Recycler tier (access-controlled): material composition, hazardous-substance disclosure, disassembly instructions, end-of-life pathway.
Regulator / customs tier (access-controlled): full compliance record, certifications, supply-chain due-diligence, conformity assessments.
All three tiers from a single physical NFC tag via SDM access-controlled file authentication.

brief.label: NFC vs QR code as DPP data carrier
items: QR code: low-cost, readable by every camera-equipped phone — fades / scratches / becomes unreadable within 2-3 years.
NFC tag: 10+ year retention; for batteries (10-15 year service) and electronics, QR cannot reliably link to DPP registry throughout regulatory lifecycle.
Cryptographic anti-counterfeit: {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} SUN mathematically prevents tag duplication; static QR is copyable.
Tap-to-access UX: consumer expectation aligned with payment / pass / verification taps in modern retail.
EU regulation does not mandate specific technology — both acceptable; NFC + QR dual carrier on premium / luxury / regulated products is the industry pattern.

brief.label: Multi-stakeholder data structure
items: Product identification: GTIN + serial number per ISO/IEC 15459.
Manufacturer information: legal entity, registered address, contact path for Article 23 / Article 47a complaint reporting.
Material composition: percentage breakdown by material class; hazardous-substance disclosure per EU REACH SVHC.
Carbon footprint: PEF (Product Environmental Footprint) method for relevant categories.
Durability + repairability: Right-to-Repair Directive 2024/1799 alignment; repairability score where required.
End-of-life: recycling instructions, recoverable-material classification, hazardous-waste handling.

brief.label: Manufacturer implementation roadmap
items: Step 1: define product data structure per EU delegated act for category.
Step 2: set up DPP data registry (hosted platform or PLM/ERP integration).
Step 3: order NFC tags with GS1 Digital Link encoding + {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} AES-128 keys.

Step 5: populate DPP registry with product data linked to each tag's unique identifier.
Step 6: test consumer access — verify tap-to-view experience on multiple phone models (iOS 14+ + Android).

sections.title: Why DPP — phased rollout, hard deadlines, and procurement lead time
bullets: Battery Passport (Reg 2023/1542) is a hard deadline at 18 February 2027 set in primary regulation — will not slip with delegated-act timing. Manufacturers in EV + industrial-storage + LMT must commit to procurement and data-registry build by Q3 2025.
Textile / electronics / furniture / construction DPP timing flows through ESPR delegated acts — phased between 2027 and 2030.

QR code labels fade within 2-3 years; NFC tags retain readability for 10+ years — for products with multi-year warranties or 10-15 year service lives, NFC is the only option that reliably outlasts the regulatory window.

sections.title: What role-based access actually unlocks

dataHighlight.heading: Consumer / recycler / regulator from a single physical NFC tag
dataHighlight.text: EU ESPR delegated acts establish that DPP data must be accessible to multiple stakeholder classes — consumers (simplified product data + repair / recycling instructions + sustainability score), recyclers (material composition + hazardous-substance disclosure + disassembly + end-of-life), regulators / customs / market-surveillance authorities (full compliance record + certifications + supply-chain due-diligence + conformity assessments). A static QR code points to a single URL — implementing role-based access requires either multiple QR codes (creating a packaging-design and consumer-confusion problem) or backend role detection (which is fragile and creates accessibility issues for unauthenticated stakeholders). {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} Secure Dynamic Messaging solves this at the chip level: each access class authenticates against a different AES-128 key, the chip returns the appropriate URL, and the brand backend serves the role-appropriate data tier. The result is a single physical NFC tag that delivers genuinely segmented stakeholder access without UX compromise. The architecture is what positions {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} as the recommended chip family for new DPP programmes; NTAG213 / 216 remain valid only where the delegated act explicitly permits public-only access throughout the product lifecycle.

sections.title: One tap, five answers — how the passport opens
sections.intro: A Digital Product Passport is only as trustworthy as the carrier it rides on, and a printed QR carries nothing it can prove. The NTAG 424 DNA chip signs a fresh URL on every tap with an AES-128 key that never leaves the silicon, so the phone resolving the GS1 Digital Link identifier is reading a passport that authenticated itself first. The full authentication mechanics live in the [NTAG 424 DNA SUN + CMAC encyclopedia](/guides/ntag424-dna-sun-cmac-authentication/); the general-purpose sibling label is the [NTAG 424 DNA TamperTag](/products/rfid-labels/ntag424-dna-tamper-evident-tag/).

image.alt: Tap-to-passport flow: a phone taps the tag at 13.56 MHz, the NTAG 424 DNA chip signs a fresh per-tap CMAC URL with its AES-128 key, the registry verifies the signature and the GS1 Digital Link resolves, and the passport opens to five data fields — origin, materials, recyclability, carbon footprint, and repair or end-of-life.

bullets: Secure Dynamic Messaging (SDM) makes the chip emit a fresh CMAC URL on every tap; the registry's tap counter rises each time, so a replayed URL is caught rather than trusted.
The AES-128 key is provisioned into the silicon at NXP's secure facility and never leaves it — cloning the label artwork or copying its URL does not reproduce the key.
No app is required: the phone OS opens the returned URL and shows the consumer view, while recycler and regulator tiers authenticate to their own keys for the deeper record.

One tap resolves the whole passport data model — GTIN and serial per ISO/IEC 15459, material composition and REACH SVHC disclosure, recyclability and end-of-life pathway, PEF carbon footprint, and repairability under Directive 2024/1799.

sections.title: Built to outlast the product — inlay construction and mounting
sections.intro: The passport has to survive everything the product does: a decade on a battery terminal, 50+ ISO 6330 wash cycles on a garment, a warranty longer than the receipt. That rules out ink. The inlay seals the NTAG 424 DNA die and its antenna behind a printed face and a tamper-evident adhesive, then mounts the way the category demands — glued, sewn, laminated in, or shrink-wrapped onto a cell. For battery packs specifically see the [NFC battery passport tag](/products/rfid-labels/nfc-battery-passport-tag/); the full form-factor range sits on the [RFID label hub](/products/rfid-labels/).

image.alt: Durable DPP inlay layer stack — printed protective face, aluminium antenna with the NTAG 424 DNA die at 13.56 MHz and AES-128 SUN, PET or woven-textile substrate, and a tamper-evident adhesive that leaves VOID on removal — with four mountings: adhesive label or hang tag, sewn-in woven tag rated to ISO 6330 50+ wash cycles and ISO 3175, embedded heat- and chemical-resistant inlay, and a battery pole label for cells over 2 kWh.

bullets: The layer stack is consistent across form factors: a printed protective face, an aluminium antenna coil carrying the NTAG 424 DNA die, a PET or woven-textile substrate, and a tamper-evident adhesive that leaves a VOID pattern if the label is peeled.

Mounting is matched to the product: adhesive label or hang tag for packaging and retail, sewn-in woven tag for garments and footwear (ISO 6330 50+ wash cycles, ISO 3175 dry-clean), embedded heat- and chemical-resistant inlay for electronics and batteries, and a battery pole label or shrink-sleeve for EV and industrial cells.
The tamper-evident construction ties the passport to the physical item — a removed or transferred tag is visible, which matters where the DPP doubles as an anti-counterfeit and provenance record.

NFC earns its place over a printed QR on durability alone: 10+ year chip retention against 2-3 year QR fade, enough to outlast the 10-15 year service life of an EV battery or a multi-year electronics warranty.

faq.question: Is NFC mandatory for DPP, or can we use QR codes?
faq.answer: EU regulation specifies that a 'data carrier' must be present on the product but does not mandate a specific technology. Both NFC and QR are acceptable. NFC is recommended where durability matters (10+ year retention vs 2-3 year QR fade), where authentication is important ({chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} prevents data-carrier counterfeiting), and where the product category will require frequent consumer interaction. Many premium / regulated programmes deploy NFC + QR dual carrier — NFC for authentication and longevity + QR for backup access by smartphones without NFC.

faq.question: What data must the DPP contain?
faq.answer: Required data varies by product category but generally includes: product identification (GTIN, serial), manufacturer information, material composition, country of manufacturing, carbon footprint data, energy efficiency (where applicable), durability and repairability information, end-of-life recycling instructions. Specific delegated acts for each product category define exact requirements. Battery Passport (Reg 2023/1542) defines its own dataset including chemistry, capacity, state-of-health, recycled-content percentages for cobalt / lithium / nickel / lead, due-diligence supply-chain information.

faq.question: Do I need to tag products sold outside the EU?
faq.answer: DPP requirement applies to products placed on the EU market regardless of where manufactured. Manufacturing in China and selling to EU = products need DPP data carriers. Products sold exclusively to non-EU markets do not require DPP compliance. However, UK (DPP framework in development), Japan, South Korea developing similar regulations, so early adoption positions for global compliance. The same NFC tag deployed for EU compliance also serves brand-protection / authentication / engagement use cases in non-EU markets.

faq.question: How does the EU Battery Regulation battery passport differ from other ESPR product categories?
faq.answer: EU Battery Regulation (2023/1542) is a standalone regulation with earlier and stricter timeline than the broader ESPR framework. Battery passport mandatory from 18 February 2027 for every LMT battery, industrial battery > 2 kWh, and EV battery placed on EU market — hard deadline set in primary regulation rather than a delegated act, will not slip in parallel with ESPR category timings. Required data includes manufacturer ID, cell chemistry, rated capacity, carbon footprint, recycled-content percentages for cobalt / lithium / nickel / lead, state-of-health, due-diligence supply-chain information. Battery manufacturers should plan 12-18 months of lead time for tag procurement, data-registry integration, production-line validation — placing the decision window in Q3 2025 for most programmes.

faq.question: Can we start with NTAG213 and upgrade to {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} once role-based access is required?
faq.answer: Physically yes, but practically usually no — switching chip families mid-programme forces re-qualification of the converting line, the tag applicator station, and the backend SDM verification stack. The more economical path for manufacturers targeting 2027-2028 deadlines: start with {chip:nxp-ntag-424-dna:short_name} on day one even if initial production run uses only a single public SDM URL. The additional per-tag cost (~USD 0.08-0.12 vs NTAG213) is small against re-validation cost, and ESPR delegated acts for textiles, electronics, batteries are all indicating role-based access requirements that will materialise within first 24 months of mandatory operation. NTAG213 remains valid only for product categories where public-only data access is explicitly sufficient per the delegated act.

faq.question: How does ERP integration work for the DPP data registry?
faq.answer: Three patterns: (1) hosted DPP platform (Circularise, EON Group, Trustchain, Trustless Computing Association reference implementations) — fastest time-to-compliance, vendor-managed; (2) ERP-integrated DPP module — SAP Asset Performance Management, Oracle Cloud SCM, Microsoft Dynamics 365 SCM all have DPP add-ons or third-party modules; (3) PLM-integrated — Siemens Teamcenter / PTC Windchill / Dassault Enovia / Aras Innovator hold bill-of-materials + material-composition data, feed DPP registry via REST API. Proud Tek provides reference implementation guidance for SAP / Oracle / Microsoft Dynamics and the hosted-platform alternatives.

faq.question: What is the MOQ, lead time and per-tag cost for DPP NFC tags?
faq.answer: MOQ is 5,000 pieces and lead time is 12-18 business days for stock antenna designs; per-tag cost runs USD 0.40-1.20 depending on chip variant and form factor. AES-128 key provisioning happens at NXP's secure facility, coordinated through the first production batch, so budget a sampling round before the production run. Across the full programme — procurement, data-registry integration and production-line validation — plan 9-18 months from decision to first production batch; battery-passport programmes facing the 18 February 2027 deadline should be committing by Q3 2025.
